title: Steering or Suspension Noise
summary: Practical chassis noise path for clunks, hums, pulls, and suspension estimate continuity.
intro: Chassis noise diagnosis starts with when the noise happens: bumps, braking, turning, road speed, or steering input each point to a different inspection path.
common_sounds: Growl or hum that changes with road speed
Wandering, pull, or uneven tire wear
quick_checks: Road test to separate bump noise from road-speed noise
Inspect control arm bushings and ball joints with suspension loaded where needed
Check wheel bearing play and tire cupping
Inspect tie rods, sway links, struts, and loose hardware

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Clunk and Loose-Joint Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Use loaded and unloaded checks to separate control arms, links, struts, and steering parts.
checks: Inspect bushing movement and ball joint play
Check sway links, tie rods, and strut mounts
Look for shiny witness marks around loose hardware

diagnostic_path_sections.title: Road-Speed Hum Path
diagnostic_path_sections.summary: Road-speed noise needs tire comparison and corner isolation before hub replacement.
checks: Compare tire wear and rotation pattern
Load each side gently during road test
Check hub roughness, play, and ABS wiring

recommended_repairs.title: Suspension Noise Diagnosis
recommended_repairs.description: Use when the noise source is not confirmed.

recommended_repairs.title: Control Arm Replacement
recommended_repairs.description: Use after bushing or ball-joint movement confirms the arm path.

recommended_repairs.title: Wheel Hub Assembly Replacement
recommended_repairs.description: Use after road-speed noise and corner isolation confirm hub failure.
